questions.question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To desire to go back to a previous point in the past to change or undo events or actions that are now regretted.

options.text: Turn back the hands of time
Arrive somewhere up on the stroke of some time

questions.solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Turn back the hands of time**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Turn back the hands of time"** means to desire to go back to a previous point in time to change or undo events or actions that are now regretted. (समय को पीछे मोड़ना चाहते हैं) • **Example:** If I could turn back the hands of time, I would undo the mistakes I made during my youth. • This idiom is metaphorical and is commonly used in situations where people express regret over past events. (भूतकाल के लिए पछतावा व्यक्त करने के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है) Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Turn back the hands of time**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 2: In the fullness of time** (समय आने पर): Refers to something happening eventually, when the time is right. • **Example:** In the fullness of time, we will see the results of our efforts. • **Option 3: Turn around time** (पलटने का समय): Refers to the time taken to complete a process or task. • **Example:** The turn-around time for repairing this device is approximately two weeks. • **Option 4: Arrive somewhere up on the stroke of some time** (सटीक समय पर पहुँचना): Refers to arriving exactly at a specific time. • **Example:** She arrived at the party on the stroke of 8 PM. 31:T9d5, The correct answer is **option 2.**

questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

To even the score.

options.text: To avenge a wrong or make an unfair situation more equal
To score a point from a particular situation or setup
To get points equal with the opponent
To be within the distance from which scoring a goal

questions.solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **To avenge a wrong or make an unfair situation more equal**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"To even the score"** means to settle a dispute or redress a wrong by avenging or rectifying an unfair situation. (गिनती बराबर करना/बदला लेना) • **Example:** After being cheated in the game, he was determined to even the score by winning the next round. • It implies taking action to make things fair or balanced, especially after being wronged. (संतुलन बनाना) • **Example:** She worked hard to even the score with her competitor in the final race. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **To avenge a wrong or make an unfair situation more equal**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 2:** **To score a point from a particular situation or setup** (किसी विशेष परिस्थिति से अंक प्राप्त करना) • **Example:** He scored a point due to his quick reflexes during the penalty shootout. • **Option 3:** **To get points equal with the opponent** (प्रतिद्वंद्वी के साथ अंक बराबर करना) • **Example:** The player evened the score by hitting a six in the last over. • **Option 4:** **To be within the distance from which scoring a goal** (गोल करने की दूरी के भीतर होना) • **Example:** The striker moved closer to the goal to be within the scoring distance. 30:T9cf, The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Turn back the hands of time**.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

Let the plot of the movie be kept a secret.

options.text: Keep the plot of the movie a secret.
The plot of the movie is a secret.
Let us kept the plot of the movie a secret.
Kept the plot of the movie a secret.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is written in passive voice, and the task is to convert it into active voice.
 
• Passive voice structure: "Let + object + be + past participle."
 
• To convert the sentence into active voice, we remove "Let" and start with the imperative verb directly.
 
• The correct active voice sentence is: "Keep the plot of the movie a secret."
 
• The verb "Keep" is in imperative form, directly addressing the subject.
 
• This conversion maintains the intended meaning of the sentence while correctly structuring it in active voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Keep the plot of the movie a secret."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "The plot of the movie is a secret." – This is not a conversion of the sentence but a different statement.
 
• **Option 3:** "Let us kept the plot of the movie a secret." – Incorrect grammar ("kept" should be "keep").
 
• **Option 4:** "Kept the plot of the movie a secret." – Incorrect sentence structure; lacks a subject.

questions.question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.

The only disadvantage with teaching is repeating the same curriculum again and again.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the preposition "**with**" after the noun "**disadvantage**."
 
• Certain nouns take specific prepositions to form a standard collocation. When referring to a drawback or a negative feature of something, the preposition "**of**" is used.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**disadvantage of teaching**," which correctly identifies the activity to which the disadvantage belongs.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The only **disadvantage of teaching** is repeating the same curriculum again and again."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The only" **– This part is grammatically correct as it functions as a determiner identifying a specific singular noun.
 
• **Option 3: "is repeating the same"** – This part is correct; "repeating" acts as a gerund serving as the subject complement.
 
• **Option 4: "curriculum again and again."** – This part is correct. While "again and again" might seem redundant with "repeating," it is a common idiomatic expression used for emphasis to show monotony.
 
• **Usage of 'Disadvantage to':** We use "disadvantage to" when referring to a person or group that is negatively affected (e.g., "The new tax is a disadvantage to low-income families").

A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: “No Improvement Required.”

The principal stated that the proposed plan was __in accordance to the guidelines__ issued by the education department.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**in accordance with the guidelines**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The phrase **"in accordance with"** is the correct usage and is commonly used to refer to compliance or agreement with a set of rules, regulations, or guidelines.
 
• The given sentence uses the incorrect phrase **"in accordance to"**, which is grammatically wrong.
 
• **Option 2: "in accordance for"** is incorrect because the preposition "for" does not fit the required grammatical structure.
 
• **Option 3: "in accordance on"** is incorrect because "on" is not appropriate in this context.
 
• **Option 4: "No improvement required"** is incorrect because the existing sentence needs improvement.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The principal stated that the proposed plan was **in accordance with the guidelines**__ issued by the education department."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "in accordance for"** is grammatically incorrect because "for" does not work with "accordance" in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "in accordance on"** is grammatically incorrect because "on" is not suitable with "accordance" here.
 
• **Option 4: No improvement required** is incorrect because the phrase "in accordance to" is wrong and needs to be replaced.
</ul

questions.question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. Soon all was quiet in the house: everyone was asleep.
A. The snowstorm had not subsided; the wind blew in their faces as if trying to stop the young criminal.
B. Her maid followed her with two bundles.
C. They descended into the garden.
D. Masha wrapped herself in a shawl, put on a warm cloak, took her small box in her hand, and went down the back staircase.
S2. With difficulty they reached the end of the garden.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentences need to be rearranged logically to maintain the coherence and unity of the paragraph.
 
• **Sentence D** introduces the action of Masha preparing to go out and descending the stairs, so it is the first logical sentence after S1.
 
• **Sentence B** follows as it describes her maid accompanying her with bundles, which logically connects to Masha preparing to leave.
 
• **Sentence C** comes next as it describes their descent into the garden, continuing the sequence of events logically.
 
• **Sentence A** is placed last before S2 as it describes the challenging weather conditions they faced after reaching the garden, leading to the final sentence.
 
• The correct sequence is **DBCA**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding the structure:** Rearranging the sentences logically involves identifying the flow of events and connections between sentences.
 
• **Key points for coherence:**
 
 
• Identify the introductory sentence that sets the scene or introduces the main action.
 
• Ensure sentences follow a logical chronological order or thematic connection.
 
• The concluding sentence should wrap up the paragraph cohesively.
 
 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Soon all was quiet in the house: everyone was asleep. Masha wrapped herself in a shawl, put on a warm cloak, took her small box in her hand, and went down the back staircase. Her maid followed her with two bundles. They descended into the garden. The snowstorm had not subsided; the wind blew in their faces as if trying to stop the young criminal. With difficulty they reached the end of the garden."</div

D. Antonio, however, appropriated no part of it to himself; he pulled off his cap exclusively to the padre, without even looking at Laurella.
S2. The scene was surely worth a moment's pause
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
 
• The paragraph revolves around Laurella's farewell and the characters Antonio and the padre, depicting their actions and emotions in a picturesque environment. 
 
• **Sentence D is the first sentence** because it describes Antonio's reaction to Laurella's farewell, showing his indifference and exclusive reverence for the padre: 
 
 
• "Antonio, however, appropriated no part of it to himself; he pulled off his cap exclusively to the padre, without even looking at Laurella." 
 
 
• **Sentence A follows** as it shows the padre and Antonio leaving, and Laurella beginning her ascent, highlighting the shift in focus: 
 
 
• "But after they had turned their backs, he let his eyes travel but a short way with the padre, as he went toiling over the deep bed of small, loose stones; he soon sent them after the maiden, who, turning to the right, had begun to climb the heights, holding one hand above her eyes to protect them from the scorching sun." 
 
 
• **Sentence C is the third sentence** because it describes Laurella pausing and looking back, adding to the vivid depiction of her journey: 
 
 
• "Just before the path disappeared behind high walls, she stopped, as if to gather breath, and looked behind her." 
 
 
• **Sentence B comes last** as it paints a picturesque view of the surroundings, emphasizing the beauty of the scene and Laurella's position: 
 
 
• "At her feet lay the marina; the rugged rocks rose high around her; the sea was shining in the rarest of its deep blue splendour." 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **DACB**. 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Antonio, however, appropriated no part of it to himself; he pulled off his cap exclusively to the padre, without even looking at Laurella. But after they had turned their backs, he let his eyes travel but a short way with the padre, as he went toiling over the deep bed of small, loose stones; he soon sent them after the maiden, who, turning to the right, had begun to climb the heights, holding one hand above her eyes to protect them from the scorching sun. Just before the path disappeared behind high walls, she stopped, as if to gather breath, and looked behind her. At her feet lay the marina; the rugged rocks rose high around her; the sea was shining in the rarest of its deep blue splendour."</div

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

I feel frustrated that she __keeps reverting back to her bad habits__ after brief phases of positive change.

options.text: keeps reverting to her bad habits
keeps reverting backward to her bad habits
keeps reverting forth to her bad habits

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**keeps reverting to her bad habits**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The word "**revert**" inherently means "to go back" or "return to a previous state," so the use of "back" in the original sentence is redundant.
 
• Option 1, "**keeps reverting to her bad habits**," removes the redundancy and provides a grammatically correct and concise sentence.
 
• Option 2 ("**keeps reverting backward to her bad habits**") repeats the redundancy by adding "backward," which is unnecessary.
 
• Option 3 ("**keeps reverting forth to her bad habits**") is incorrect because "reverting forth" is not a valid usage of the verb "revert."
 
• Option 4 ("**No improvement required**") is incorrect because the original sentence contains redundancy that needs to be corrected.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"I feel frustrated that she **keeps reverting to her bad habits**__ after brief phases of positive change."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "keeps reverting backward to her bad habits" is incorrect because "reverting" already implies going back, making "backward" redundant.
 
• **Option 3:** "keeps reverting forth to her bad habits" is incorrect because "reverting forth" does not make sense in standard English usage.
 
• **Option 4:** "No improvement required" is incorrect because the original sentence has a redundancy that needs correction.

questions.question: What does the fox symbolize in Ted Hughes’ poem The Thought Fox?

options.text: The writer’s loneliness and disconnection with nature
The slowly emerging imaginative power and creative inspiration in the writer’s mind
The nature’s destructive power that hinders the poet's writing
The factory development that eclipses the countryside and art.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ***Option 2: The slowly emerging imaginative power and creative inspiration in the writer’s mind.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly states that the fox **"represents the poet's imaginative powers"** and the **"symbolism of poetic inspiration."**

questions.question: Why does the poet describe a sense of loneliness in the poem?

options.text: As he is going through a dry creative period, even though he is in the middle of a crowd.
As he is literally pushed away in a forest far from any human being.
As he considers himself an outsider to the social group and does not want to interact with anyone at all.
As he remembers the good old days of his childhood, he longs for the countryside life very much.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: As he is going through a dry creative period, even though he is in the middle of a crowd.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly clarifies the nature of the poet's isolation: **"this loneliness is not the absence of people around him, but the absence of Creative powers."**
 
• A "dry creative period" is a common literary way to describe the **absence of inspiration** or "Creative powers" mentioned in the text. Even if people are physically present, the poet feels "lonely" because he cannot connect with his own imagination.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: As he is literally pushed away in a forest far from any human being.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage states that the fox is an **image** or **symbol** and that the loneliness is specifically *not* about the physical absence of people.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: As he considers himself an outsider to the social group...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text focuses entirely on the **process of poetic inspiration** and the "blank pages," rather than the poet's social standing or his desire to interact with others.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: As he remembers the good old days of his childhood...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. There is no mention of childhood, nostalgia, or a longing for the countryside life in the provided passage.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Writer's Block**: The phrase "his fingers move, but the pages remain blank" is a classic description of writer's block. The "loneliness" here is the frustration of having the tools to write but lacking the internal "spark."
 
• **Symbolic Fox**: The fox is the **thought** that gradually becomes solid. Just as a fox's nose or eyes might appear first in the darkness of a forest, a poem often begins with a single, small image or "part" before the whole idea is formed.
 
• **Loneliness as a Catalyst**: For many poets, this "special kind of loneliness" is necessary for the imagination to take shape, as it forces the mind to look inward for the "fox" to appear.

questions.question: How does the poem illustrate the process of writing a literary composition?

options.text: By demonstrating that poems are generally composed in a single session, with a constant and uninterrupted flow of ideas
By implying that creativity is a systematic process and adheres to a standardized formula
By representing inspiration as being cut up into pieces, coming bit by bit, before a whole thought is formed
By drawing attention to the fact that poetic ideas arrive already shaped, with no work or time needed

The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

• ***Option 3: By representing inspiration as being cut up into pieces, coming bit by bit, before a whole thought is formed.***

 
 
• According to the passage, the poem serves as a **"perfect illustration"** of how inspiration arrives. It emphasizes that **"any literary composition is produced in parts."**

questions.question: What is the significance of animal imagery in The Thought Fox?

options.text: It gives a bright picture of the countryside, not connected to the theme of creativity
It highlights the anxiety of the poet in regard to nature and its unpredictability
It points out the drawbacks of industrialization in relation to nature and its inhabitants.
It hides the abstract idea of poetic inspiration under a visible, palatable metaphor

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 4: It hides the abstract idea of poetic inspiration under a visible, palatable metaphor.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly states that **"the symbolism of poetic inspiration is concealed behind the animal imagery."**
 
• Poetic inspiration is an **abstract** concept (something that cannot be seen or touched). By using the **fox** as a metaphor, Ted Hughes makes this abstract process **visible** and **palatable** (easier to understand or digest) for the reader.
 
• The "part-by-part" description of the fox (nose, eyes, prints) serves as a physical representation of how a poem gradually takes shape in the mind.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: It gives a bright picture of the countryside...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage confirms that the imagery is directly **"symbolic of the process of poetic inspiration,"** contradicting the idea that it is not connected to the theme of creativity.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: It highlights the anxiety of the poet in regard to nature...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While there is a sense of "loneliness" mentioned, it is a **creative loneliness** (the absence of ideas), not an anxiety about the unpredictability of nature itself.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: It points out the drawbacks of industrialization...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage does not discuss industrialization, factories, or environmental drawbacks. It focuses entirely on **literary composition**.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metaphor vs. Symbol**: A metaphor directly compares two unlike things. Here, the fox *is* the thought. As a symbol, the fox represents the wild, untameable, and sudden nature of a **creative spark**.
 
• **Animal Poetry**: Ted Hughes is known as an "animal poet." He often used animals to bridge the gap between the **human intellect** and the **instinctual world**.
 
• **The "Internal" Forest**: In the poem, the setting is both a literal dark night and a metaphorical "forest" of the poet's mind where the "Thought Fox" lives.

questions.question: Why is The Thought Fox considered one of Hughes’ most celebrated early poems?

options.text: For the reason that it deals with the poet's intimate relations rather than his art in the making
Since the poem deals with the themes of the countryside and the industrialization of Northern Ireland
Due to the fact that it reveals the mystery of the creative process by means of abundant, vivid imagery
As the poem does not use metaphors at all and only gives a literal account of the situation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 3: Due to the fact that it reveals the mystery of the creative process by means of abundant, vivid imagery.***

 
 
• The passage describes the poem as a **"perfect illustration"** of how poetic inspiration comes to a writer.
 
• It "reveals the mystery" by showing that inspiration is not a sudden, complete event but a **gradual process**, which Hughes captures through **"vivid imagery"** of the fox appearing part by part (nose, eyes, prints).
 
• The use of the fox as a symbol for **imaginative powers** is what makes the poem a celebrated early work.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: For the reason that it deals with the poet's intimate relations...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage explicitly states that the poem is about **"the process of poetic inspiration"** (art in the making) rather than the poet's personal or intimate relationships.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Since the poem deals with the themes of the countryside and industrialization...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While Ted Hughes often wrote about the countryside, this specific passage makes no mention of **industrialization** or Northern Ireland.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: As the poem does not use metaphors at all...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text clarifies that the poem is **"symbolic"** and that the imagery **"conceals"** the meaning, which is the definition of metaphorical writing.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Animal as Idea**: In "The Thought Fox," the fox is not a real animal in a literal forest; it is an **idea** emerging from the "forest" of the poet's mind.
 
• **Creative Loneliness**: The passage emphasizes that the poet's "loneliness" is a necessary state for **creation**. Without this space, the "fox" of inspiration cannot find its way to the page.
 
• **Vividness**: By using specific body parts of the fox (nose, eyes), Hughes makes the internal **act of thinking** feel as real and physical as an animal walking through the snow.
